heading: EXT. SALT-LICK STAGE STATION - NEVADA TERRITORY - DAY

units.text: EXT. SALT-LICK STAGE STATION - NEVADA TERRITORY - DAY
A dusty way station with a sagging porch, a hand-pump well, and a corral.
A white salt flat shimmers beyond.
A stagecoach rests with its team unhitched, horses nosing at a lick of gray rock.
On the porch sits OLD CASPER VANDERHOOF, 70s, in a rocker, whittling.
Beside him, his granddaughter LUPE, 10, dangles bare feet off the boards.
Across the yard the stagecoach driver, TOMÁS ESCOBEDO, 40s, leans against a wheel, hat tipped over his eyes.
A passenger, the preacher JEDEDIAH HOLLOWAY, 50s, stands at the pump filling a canteen.
Inside the open stagecoach door, the passenger MRS. PRUDENCE LATIMER, 30s, fans herself with a handkerchief.
At the corral rail, a ranch hand named WYATT BROOKS, 20s, scratches a mule's ear.
Nobody hurries.
A hawk circles overhead.
Casper's knife shaves a long curl off the stick.
Lupe watches it fall.
Grandpa, what's it going to be?
units.name: LUPE

units.text: A duck.
units.name: CASPER

units.text: It looks like a spoon.
units.name: LUPE

units.text: That's a duck in a hurry.
units.name: CASPER

units.text: Tomás pushes up his hat and glances at the sun.
Jedediah finishes with the canteen and pumps the handle twice more just to hear it creak.
Prudence steps down from the coach, shakes the dust from her skirt, and crosses to the porch, handing the handkerchief to Lupe, who wipes her nose and hands it back with great seriousness.
Wyatt gives the mule a last pat and ambles over to join them, thumbs in his belt.
Will she be rolling by noon?
units.name: WYATT

units.text: When the horses finish licking.
units.name: TOMÁS

units.text: Shame to rush them.
units.name: WYATT

units.text: The Lord rested on the seventh day.
units.name: JEDEDIAH

units.text: The Lord didn't have a schedule from the railroad.
units.name: TOMÁS

units.text: Then let us rest, gentlemen. I have nowhere I would rather not be.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Spoken like a woman who's seen Reno.
units.name: CASPER

units.text: Twice.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: The hawk drifts lower.
Lupe points.
Everyone looks up.
For a long moment the whole station watches the bird wheel against the bright sky, and then it banks and is gone over the flat.
That's a duck, too.
units.name: CASPER

units.text: It's not.
units.name: LUPE

units.text: It's a duck in a hurry.
units.name: CASPER
